hebreus-sem-hb-01-01.question: In Hebrews 1:1, God spoke long ago to the fathers through the prophets.
hebreus-sem-hb-01-01.feedbackCorrect: Long ago, God spoke many times and in many ways, through the prophets.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Hebrews 1:1 and see through whom God spoke long ago.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-01.hint: See through whom God spoke in ancient times.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-02.question: In Hebrews 1:3, tap who sustains all things.
hebreus-sem-hb-01-02.feedbackCorrect: He, the Son, sustains all things by the word of his power.

feedbackWrong.a: The word is the means; the one who sustains is a person.
feedbackWrong.b: The Majesty is the one at whose right hand the Son sits, not the one who sustains.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-02.hint: Look for who performs the action at the start of the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-03.question: According to Hebrews 1:4, the Son became superior to whom?
hebreus-sem-hb-01-03.feedbackCorrect: The name the Son inherited is more excellent than that of the angels.

feedbackWrong.a: The universe was made through him; it is not compared to him here.
feedbackWrong.b: The prophets spoke for God, but the comparison here is with other beings.
feedbackWrong.c: The fathers heard through the prophets; they are not the point of comparison.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-03.hint: Read to see with whom the Son's name is compared.

options.a: The created universe
options.b: The prophets of the past
options.c: The fathers of faith

hebreus-sem-hb-01-04.question: Put Hebrews 1:1 in the order of the text.
hebreus-sem-hb-01-04.feedbackCorrect: First the ancient speech through the prophets; finally, the speech through the Son.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the ancient speech; the speech through the Son closes the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-04.hint: The speech through the Son comes at the end of the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-05.question: In Hebrews 1:2, God appointed the Son as what of all things?
hebreus-sem-hb-01-05.feedbackCorrect: The Son is the heir of all things, not just another servant.

feedbackWrong.a: Servants follow orders; the Son is presented as heir.
feedbackWrong.b: Prophets spoke for God; the Son receives everything as inheritance.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-05.hint: See what the Son receives from God in the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-06.question: What does Hebrews 1:6 say that connects to this context?
hebreus-sem-hb-01-06.feedbackCorrect: The angels worship the Son: they serve him, not the other way around.

feedbackWrong.a: The one in command is God, when he presents the Firstborn into the world.
feedbackWrong.c: The angels worship the Son; no one takes his place.

hebreus-sem-hb-01-06.hint: See what God commands the angels to do.

options.a: The angels command the Son
options.b: The angels worship the Son
options.c: The angels replace the Son

hebreus-cam-hb-01-01.question: In Hebrews 1:1, God spoke to the fathers through the Son many times and in many ways.
hebreus-cam-hb-01-01.feedbackCorrect: Many times and in many ways was through the prophets; through the Son, in these days.

feedbackWrong.true: Swap the messengers: many times was through the prophets, not the Son.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-01.hint: Separate the ancient speech from the speech of the last days.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-02.question: In Hebrews 1:1, tap the word that marks the ancient time of God's speech.
hebreus-cam-hb-01-02.feedbackCorrect: That word opens the ancient time, before the speech through the Son.

feedbackWrong.b: Prophets are the messengers of that time, not the time marker.
feedbackWrong.c: The Son marks the last days, the other side of the contrast.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-02.hint: Look for the time word right after God's name.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-03.question: How does Hebrews 1:1 connect God's ancient speech to his speech through the Son?
hebreus-cam-hb-01-03.feedbackCorrect: There is a before through the prophets and a now through the Son, with no silence between.

feedbackWrong.a: To the fathers, God spoke through the prophets; the Son comes in the last days.
feedbackWrong.b: God did not fall silent: in these last days, he spoke to us through the Son.
feedbackWrong.d: The order is reversed: first the prophets, then the Son.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-03.hint: Compare the time of the prophets with the time of the Son.

options.a: The Son spoke to the fathers in ancient times
options.b: God stopped speaking after the prophets
options.c: God spoke before through prophets and now through the Son
options.d: The prophets spoke after the Son came

hebreus-cam-hb-01-04.question: How does the argument advance in Hebrews 1:1–2?
hebreus-cam-hb-01-04.feedbackCorrect: From the ancient speech, the text arrives at the Son and shows his place.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the prophets; the heir appears after the speech through the Son.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-04.hint: The Son as heir appears in the second verse.

options.a: God spoke long ago through the prophets
options.b: God speaks now through the Son
options.c: The Son is heir of everything

hebreus-cam-hb-01-05.question: In Hebrews 1:3, all things are sustained by the word of which attribute of the Son?
hebreus-cam-hb-01-05.feedbackCorrect: The Son sustains everything by the word of his power, effortlessly.

feedbackWrong.a: Sin is what he cleanses, not the means of sustaining all things.
feedbackWrong.b: Glory appears at the start of the verse, tied to the radiance.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-05.hint: Read the middle of the verse, about sustaining.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-06.question: What connects Hebrews 1:5 to Psalm 2:7?
hebreus-cam-hb-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews quotes the Psalm: God said these words only to the Son.

feedbackWrong.a: The speaker in the Psalm is God, calling someone his Son.
feedbackWrong.b: The text asks to which angel God ever said this: to none.

hebreus-cam-hb-01-06.hint: See whom God calls this in both texts.

options.a: The prophets beget the Son
options.b: An angel receives this name
options.c: God calls Jesus his Son

hebreus-pro-hb-01-01.question: Hebrews 1:3 presents the Son as the exact representation of God's being.
hebreus-pro-hb-01-01.feedbackCorrect: Whoever sees the Son sees exactly who God is, without a shadow.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Hebrews 1:3 about the radiance and the representation.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-01.hint: Look at how the verse describes the Son.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-02.question: In Hebrews 1:3, tap the word that shows the Son revealing God's glory.
hebreus-pro-hb-01-02.feedbackCorrect: As brightness reveals the sun, the Son reveals God's glory.

feedbackWrong.a: Heights is the place where he sits, at the end of the verse.
feedbackWrong.b: That word speaks of sins, not of revealing glory.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-02.hint: Look for the image of light at the start of the verse.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-03.question: What reading do Hebrews 1:4–6 support about the Son and the angels?
hebreus-pro-hb-01-03.feedbackCorrect: The Son inherited a greater name, and the angels worship him by God's order.

feedbackWrong.a: God never called an angel Son; the Son is above them.
feedbackWrong.c: The one who speaks at last is the Son; the angels worship him, not replace him.
feedbackWrong.d: The Son's name is more excellent than theirs, not equal.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-03.hint: Put together the inherited name and the order given to the angels.

options.a: The Son is the greatest angel created by God
options.b: The Son is superior and the angels worship him
options.c: The angels speak in place of the Son today
options.d: The angels have the same name as the Son

hebreus-pro-hb-01-04.question: Which sequence reveals the Son's path in Hebrews 1:3?
hebreus-pro-hb-01-04.feedbackCorrect: Reveal God, cleanse sins and sit down: the Son's complete work.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the verse: reveal, cleanse and only then sit down.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-04.hint: Sitting down comes after the cleansing, in the text.

options.a: The Son reveals who God is
options.b: He cleanses sins
options.c: He sits down on high

hebreus-pro-hb-01-05.question: In Hebrews 1:3, what did the Son do about sins before sitting down?
hebreus-pro-hb-01-05.feedbackCorrect: He made purification for sins and then sat down on high.

feedbackWrong.b: Worship is what the angels give him, not what he does about sins.
feedbackWrong.c: Separation is not the text's word for what he did.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-05.hint: Read the part of the verse before the sitting down.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-06.question: What connects Hebrews 1:2 to John 1:3?
hebreus-pro-hb-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Both texts say everything was made through him.

feedbackWrong.a: Prophets spoke for God; the one who made the universe was the Son.
feedbackWrong.c: Nothing came about on its own: everything was made through the Son.

hebreus-pro-hb-01-06.hint: See through whom everything was made in both texts.

options.a: The prophets created the world
options.b: Christ made all things
options.c: The universe came about on its own

hebreus-sem-hb-02-01.question: In Hebrews 4:15, Jesus was tempted in all things but without sin.
hebreus-sem-hb-02-01.feedbackCorrect: He knows temptation from the inside, without ever having given in to sin.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Hebrews 4:15 to the end and see how his temptation ends.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-01.hint: Read the whole verse, to the last part.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-02.question: In Hebrews 4:15, tap what the high priest sympathizes with in us.
hebreus-sem-hb-02-02.feedbackCorrect: He sympathizes with our weaknesses because he has already been through the test.

feedbackWrong.a: Sin is precisely what he did not have, at the end of the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: Things is too broad a word; the text names something of ours.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-02.hint: Read the first part of the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-03.question: According to Hebrews 4:14, what did Jesus, the Son of God, do in the heavens?
hebreus-sem-hb-02-03.feedbackCorrect: He passed through the heavens: he entered God's presence for his people.

feedbackWrong.b: The text places him beyond the heavens, not waiting on earth.
feedbackWrong.c: Rest is an earlier theme; here the focus is the priest in the heavens.
feedbackWrong.d: He himself is the great high priest; he does not hand over the office.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-03.hint: See where the great high priest has already arrived.

options.a: He passed through the heavens as high priest
options.b: He stayed waiting on earth with the disciples
options.c: He went down to the rest of the ancient patriarchs
options.d: He handed the priesthood to other men

hebreus-sem-hb-02-04.question: Put Hebrews 4:16 in the order of the text.
hebreus-sem-hb-02-04.feedbackCorrect: Come, receive mercy and find grace: in that order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the invitation to come; the help closes the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-04.hint: The verse starts with an invitation.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-05.question: In Hebrews 4:16, how should we approach the throne of grace?
hebreus-sem-hb-02-05.feedbackCorrect: We come with confidence because the one who receives us sympathizes with us.

feedbackWrong.a: The invitation is precisely the opposite of coming in fear.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of rushing, but of the attitude of the heart.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-05.hint: See the attitude asked for right after the invitation.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-06.question: What does Hebrews 4:15 say that connects to this context?
hebreus-sem-hb-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Tempted as we are, he sympathizes instead of pulling away.

feedbackWrong.a: He was tempted in all things, as we are.
feedbackWrong.c: To sympathize is the opposite of ignoring those who suffer.

hebreus-sem-hb-02-06.hint: See what he feels toward our weaknesses.

options.a: He was never tested
options.b: He understands our weakness
options.c: He ignores our weakness

hebreus-cam-hb-02-01.question: In Hebrews 4:14, we have a distant high priest who does not know our life.
hebreus-cam-hb-02-01.feedbackCorrect: He is in the heavens and, at the same time, sympathizes with our weaknesses.

feedbackWrong.true: Put the two verses together: in the heavens, yes; distant from us, no.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-01.hint: Do not stop at verse 14; read the next one.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-02.question: In Hebrews 4:12, tap the word that introduces the reason for what comes before.
hebreus-cam-hb-02-02.feedbackCorrect: That word opens the explanation about the power of God's word.

feedbackWrong.a: Soul appears in the middle of the verse, in the effect of the word.
feedbackWrong.b: Sword is the image used later, not the opening connection.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-02.hint: It is the first word of the verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-03.question: How does Hebrews 4:12 relate to the effort asked for in 4:11?
hebreus-cam-hb-02-03.feedbackCorrect: The living word discerns the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

feedbackWrong.a: The text asks for effort precisely because the word works in us.
feedbackWrong.c: It pierces and discerns the heart, far beyond ancient facts.
feedbackWrong.d: Effort responds to the word; it does not take its place.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-03.hint: See what the word does inside a person.

options.a: The word makes any effort by the reader unnecessary
options.b: The living word reveals the heart of the listener
options.c: The word serves only to know ancient facts
options.d: Human effort replaces the word of God

hebreus-cam-hb-02-04.question: How does the argument advance in Hebrews 4:14–15?
hebreus-cam-hb-02-04.feedbackCorrect: First who we have, then the call to hold firm, and the reason in him.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the high priest; the compassion comes in the next verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-04.hint: The compassion closes the passage, in verse 15.

options.a: We have a high priest in the heavens
options.b: Let us hold firm our confession
options.c: He sympathizes with our weaknesses

hebreus-cam-hb-02-05.question: In Hebrews 4:14, how should we hold on to our confession?
hebreus-cam-hb-02-05.feedbackCorrect: We hold the confession firmly because the priest has already entered the heavens.

feedbackWrong.a: Letting go of the confession is the opposite of the text's call.
feedbackWrong.c: The text calls us to hold on to the confession, not to silence it.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-06.question: What connects Hebrews 4:15 to Hebrews 2:17?
hebreus-cam-hb-02-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, he became like us in order to be merciful.

feedbackWrong.a: He sympathizes with weaknesses; he is not far from those who suffer.
feedbackWrong.c: Mercy is precisely the center of both passages.

hebreus-cam-hb-02-06.hint: See what both passages say about him and us.

options.a: A priest far from those who suffer
options.b: A priest who knows our trials
options.c: A priest with no mercy at all

hebreus-pro-hb-02-01.question: Hebrews 4:16 teaches that only those without weaknesses can approach the throne of grace.
hebreus-pro-hb-02-01.feedbackCorrect: The invitation is to receive mercy, precisely for those who need it.

feedbackWrong.true: The throne is of grace: one comes to receive help, not because one deserves it.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-01.hint: See what is received upon approaching the throne.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-02.question: In Hebrews 4:15, tap the phrase that shows the difference between Jesus and us in the test.
hebreus-pro-hb-02-02.feedbackCorrect: Tempted like us in everything, he is the only one who never sinned.

feedbackWrong.b: Weaknesses are what he feels for us, not what sets him apart.
feedbackWrong.c: That shows the likeness in the test, not the final difference.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-02.hint: Look for the end of the verse, after the likeness.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-03.question: What reading do Hebrews 4:14–16 support about approaching God?
hebreus-pro-hb-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Confidence is born of a priest who knows weakness without sinning.

feedbackWrong.b: The invitation is to come to receive grace, not after overcoming everything.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of help in time of need, not of the absence of trials.
feedbackWrong.d: Those who come are precisely those who were tested and need help.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-03.hint: Connect his compassion to the invitation of verse 16.

options.a: We can come confidently because he sympathizes
options.b: We should wait to become strong and then pray
options.c: God's help always comes before the trial
options.d: God receives only those who were never tempted

hebreus-pro-hb-02-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path opened in Hebrews 4:15–16?
hebreus-pro-hb-02-04.feedbackCorrect: Because he overcame the trial, we come and receive help in time.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the trial overcome; help is the point of arrival.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-04.hint: Help in time of need closes the path.

options.a: He was tempted without sinning
options.b: Let us come confidently to the throne
options.c: We receive grace at the right time

hebreus-pro-hb-02-05.question: In Hebrews 4:16, what do we receive first when we approach the throne of grace?
hebreus-pro-hb-02-05.feedbackCorrect: We receive mercy and find grace as timely help.

feedbackWrong.a: The throne here is of grace, not of condemnation for those who come.
feedbackWrong.c: Rest is the theme of 4:11; here the gift named is different.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-05.hint: Read the part of the verse after coming.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-06.question: What connects Hebrews 4:16 to Ephesians 3:12?
hebreus-pro-hb-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul and Hebrews speak of the same confident access to God in Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: Both texts call us to come near, not to flee in fear.
feedbackWrong.c: Access is for those who believe, through Jesus, not just for one group.

hebreus-pro-hb-02-06.hint: See the attitude with which one approaches God in both.

options.a: Access to God with confidence
options.b: Fear when approaching God
options.c: Access only for priests

hebreus-sem-hb-03-01.question: In Hebrews 8:6, Jesus is mediator of a superior covenant.
hebreus-sem-hb-03-01.feedbackCorrect: He has a more excellent ministry and mediates this covenant.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Hebrews 8:6 and see Jesus' role in the covenant.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-01.hint: See Jesus' role in the middle of the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-02.question: In Hebrews 8:6, tap Jesus' role between God and the people.
hebreus-sem-hb-03-02.feedbackCorrect: He is the mediator: he stands between God and the people in this covenant.

feedbackWrong.a: Ministry is his service; the role between God and the people is another.
feedbackWrong.b: Promises are the basis of the covenant, not Jesus' role in it.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-02.hint: Look for who connects God to the people in the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-03.question: According to Hebrews 8:5, what is the service of the ancient priests like?
hebreus-sem-hb-03-03.feedbackCorrect: Their service showed the form of heaven, without being heaven itself.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses was instructed by God when building the tabernacle.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus' ministry is far more excellent than this service.
feedbackWrong.d: Copy and shadow point to the reality; they are not the reality itself.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-03.hint: Read the start of the verse about how they minister.

options.a: A human invention without divine command
options.b: A service greater than Jesus' in heaven
options.c: A copy and shadow of heavenly things
options.d: The final reality coming from heaven to earth

hebreus-sem-hb-03-04.question: Put Hebrews 8:8 in the order of the text.
hebreus-sem-hb-03-04.feedbackCorrect: Days are coming, God establishes the covenant, and the people are Israel and Judah.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the announcement of the days; the people appear at the end.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-04.hint: The verse begins with an announcement from God.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-05.question: In Hebrews 8:6, the covenant mediated by Jesus is greater in what sense?
hebreus-sem-hb-03-05.feedbackCorrect: It is a superior covenant, above the first in promises and effect.

feedbackWrong.a: The text calls it superior and more excellent, not lesser.
feedbackWrong.b: Old is precisely the earlier covenant, not this one.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-05.hint: See how the verse describes this covenant.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-06.question: What does Hebrews 8:8 say that connects to this context?
hebreus-sem-hb-03-06.feedbackCorrect: It is God who says he will establish the new covenant with Israel and Judah.

feedbackWrong.a: Giving up would be the opposite of establishing a new covenant.
feedbackWrong.c: God is the one who establishes: the promise comes from him, not the people.

hebreus-sem-hb-03-06.hint: See who promises and what he promises to do.

options.a: God gives up on his people
options.b: God promises a new covenant
options.c: The people create a new covenant

hebreus-cam-hb-03-01.question: In Hebrews 8:6, Jesus' ministry is far more excellent than the old one.
hebreus-cam-hb-03-01.feedbackCorrect: His ministry is far more excellent than the old service.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Hebrews 8:6 and see the degree of his ministry.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-01.hint: See the degree of Jesus' ministry in verse 6.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-02.question: In Hebrews 8:5, tap the word that connects Moses' work to the pattern on the mountain.
hebreus-cam-hb-03-02.feedbackCorrect: Everything had to be made according to the pattern shown to Moses.

feedbackWrong.a: Mountain is the place of the pattern, not the connecting word.
feedbackWrong.c: Shadow describes the service, not the link to the pattern.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-02.hint: Look for the word before it speaks of the pattern.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-03.question: How does Hebrews 8:7 explain the coming of a second covenant?
hebreus-cam-hb-03-03.feedbackCorrect: If the first had been enough, no second would have been sought.

feedbackWrong.a: The one who establishes the new covenant is God, as he promised.
feedbackWrong.b: The text gives the reason: the first was not without fault.
feedbackWrong.c: The first existed; the point is that it was not without fault.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-03.hint: Read the condition the verse presents.

options.a: The people invented a better covenant on their own
options.b: God changed his mind for no stated reason
options.c: The first covenant never truly existed
options.d: The first was not without fault, so another came

hebreus-cam-hb-03-04.question: How does the argument advance in Hebrews 8:5–6?
hebreus-cam-hb-03-04.feedbackCorrect: From the ancient shadow, the text arrives at Jesus' excellent ministry.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the ancient copy; the mediator closes the movement.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-04.hint: The mediator of the superior covenant comes last.

options.a: The ancient service is a copy and shadow
options.b: Jesus receives a more excellent ministry
options.c: He mediates a superior covenant

hebreus-cam-hb-03-05.question: In Hebrews 8:8, what kind of covenant does God say he will establish?
hebreus-cam-hb-03-05.feedbackCorrect: God promises to establish a new covenant, different from the old one.

feedbackWrong.a: Old would be repeating the earlier one; God announces something new.
feedbackWrong.b: The promise is announced to the people, not hidden from them.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-05.hint: See the adjective God uses for the covenant.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-06.question: What connects Hebrews 8:8 to Jeremiah 31:31?
hebreus-cam-hb-03-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews quotes Jeremiah's promise about days that would come.

feedbackWrong.a: It is precisely a new promise being fulfilled, not the end of them.
feedbackWrong.c: The promise looks ahead, to Israel and Judah, not only to the past.

hebreus-cam-hb-03-06.hint: See what God promises in both texts.

options.a: The end of every promise
options.b: The promised new covenant
options.c: A covenant only with the fathers

hebreus-pro-hb-03-01.question: Hebrews 8:9 presents the new covenant as identical to the one made with the fathers in Egypt.
hebreus-pro-hb-03-01.feedbackCorrect: The text itself says it will not be like the covenant of Egypt.

feedbackWrong.true: The verse begins by denying: not like the covenant made with the fathers.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-01.hint: Read the first words of verse 9.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-02.question: In Hebrews 8:7, tap the phrase that shows the limit of the first covenant.
hebreus-pro-hb-03-02.feedbackCorrect: The first was not without fault; therefore another was sought.

feedbackWrong.a: Second is the covenant that came, not the limit of the first.
feedbackWrong.b: That names the covenant, but does not show its limit.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-02.hint: Look for what the first would have had to be to suffice.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-03.question: What reading do Hebrews 8:3–6 support about the ancient service?
hebreus-pro-hb-03-03.feedbackCorrect: Copy and shadow have value: they show the form of what is greater.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus' ministry is far more excellent than this service.
feedbackWrong.b: It pointed ahead; the excellent ministry was still to come.
feedbackWrong.d: Moses acted by divine instruction, according to the pattern on the mountain.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-03.hint: Think about what a shadow does in relation to the real thing.

options.a: It was greater than Jesus' ministry
options.b: It was the end of the story of worship of God
options.c: It was a shadow pointing to something greater
options.d: It was a human invention of no value to God

hebreus-pro-hb-03-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Hebrews 8:6–7?
hebreus-pro-hb-03-04.feedbackCorrect: The limit of the first opens the way to the covenant mediated by Jesus.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the limit of the first; the mediator is the arrival.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-04.hint: The fault of the first comes before the search for the second.

options.a: The first was not without fault
options.b: A second covenant was sought
options.c: Jesus mediates the superior covenant

hebreus-pro-hb-03-05.question: In Hebrews 8:6, the superior covenant was established on promises of what kind?
hebreus-pro-hb-03-05.feedbackCorrect: Better promises support a covenant superior to the first.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not measure the promises by size, but by quality.
feedbackWrong.c: First would be those of the old covenant, not of this one.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-06.question: What connects Hebrews 8:6 to Luke 22:20?
hebreus-pro-hb-03-06.feedbackCorrect: At the supper, Jesus calls the cup the new covenant in his blood.

feedbackWrong.a: Hebrews names the mediator: the covenant was not left without one.
feedbackWrong.b: Luke speaks of Jesus' blood, not of animals forever.

hebreus-pro-hb-03-06.hint: See what Jesus says about the cup at the supper.

options.a: A covenant with no mediator at all
options.b: The blood of animals forever
options.c: A new covenant in Jesus' blood

hebreus-sem-hb-04-01.question: In Hebrews 11:1, faith is doubt about the things hoped for.
hebreus-sem-hb-04-01.feedbackCorrect: Faith is assurance of what is hoped for, not doubt about it.

feedbackWrong.true: Swap the central word: the text speaks of assurance, not doubt.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-01.hint: Compare the statement with the first word after faith.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-02.question: In Hebrews 11:1, tap the first mark of faith regarding what is hoped for.
hebreus-sem-hb-04-02.feedbackCorrect: Faith is assurance of the things hoped for, before seeing them.

feedbackWrong.b: Realities are the object of the conviction, not the first mark.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the second mark, tied to what is not seen.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-02.hint: Read the first half of the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-03.question: According to Hebrews 11:2, what did the ancients gain by faith?
hebreus-sem-hb-04-03.feedbackCorrect: By faith, the ancients received God's approval over their lives.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not promise riches as a direct fruit of faith here.
feedbackWrong.b: The chapter includes suffering; faith is not an exemption from pain.
feedbackWrong.c: The testimony is before God, not fame among the nations.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-03.hint: See what faith gained for the ancients.

options.a: Riches and lands without any effort
options.b: Exemption from any future suffering
options.c: A famous name among all peoples

hebreus-sem-hb-04-04.question: Put Hebrews 11:1 in the order of the text.
hebreus-sem-hb-04-04.feedbackCorrect: Assurance of what is hoped for and conviction of what is not seen.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with assurance; what is not seen closes the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-04.hint: The verse begins by defining faith.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-05.question: In Hebrews 11:1, faith is assurance of things that do what?
hebreus-sem-hb-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Faith is certain precisely of what is still hoped for.

feedbackWrong.a: Seeing is the opposite of the point here: faith reaches what is not seen.
feedbackWrong.b: Touching is not the text's word for these things.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-05.hint: Think about what is still in the future.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-06.question: What does Hebrews 11:4 say that connects to this context?
hebreus-sem-hb-04-06.feedbackCorrect: By faith, Abel offered God a more excellent sacrifice.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says the opposite: Abel's offering was more excellent.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse begins by linking Abel's offering to his faith.

hebreus-sem-hb-04-06.hint: See the first two words of the verse.

options.a: Cain offers better than Abel
options.b: Abel offers with faith
options.c: Abel offers without faith

hebreus-cam-hb-04-01.question: In Hebrews 11:3, what is visible was made from what was also visible.
hebreus-cam-hb-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The visible was made from things that are not seen, by the word.

feedbackWrong.true: Reverse the end of the verse: the visible came from what is not seen.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-01.hint: Read the end of verse 3 carefully.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-02.question: In Hebrews 11:3, tap the phrase that opens the statement about understanding creation.
hebreus-cam-hb-04-02.feedbackCorrect: It is by faith that we understand how the worlds were formed.

feedbackWrong.b: The word is the means of creation, not the opening of the statement.
feedbackWrong.c: Visible is the result, at the end of the verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-02.hint: It is how the verse begins.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-03.question: How does Hebrews 11:1–2 connect the definition of faith to the ancients?
hebreus-cam-hb-04-03.feedbackCorrect: The definition gains faces: the ancients lived it and were approved.

feedbackWrong.a: It was precisely by faith that they gained a good testimony.
feedbackWrong.b: Faith is conviction of what is not seen, for them too.
feedbackWrong.c: The ancients already lived by faith, before us.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-03.hint: See what happened to those who lived the definition.

options.a: The ancients lived without needing to trust anything
options.b: The ancients saw everything before trusting God
options.c: Faith began only after ancient times
options.d: Those who lived this way received God's approval

hebreus-cam-hb-04-04.question: How does the argument advance in Hebrews 11:1–2?
hebreus-cam-hb-04-04.feedbackCorrect: Definition first; then the ancients as living proof of it.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the definition; the ancients come in the next verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-04.hint: The ancients appear only in the second verse.

options.a: Faith is assured of what it hopes for
options.b: Faith convinces of what is not seen
options.c: The ancients receive a good testimony

hebreus-cam-hb-04-05.question: In Hebrews 11:2, the ancients gained by faith a good what?
hebreus-cam-hb-04-05.feedbackCorrect: The good testimony is God's approval over their lives.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of a trophy, but of God's approval.
feedbackWrong.c: No empire is promised to the ancients in this verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-05.hint: See what God says about their lives.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-06.question: What connects Hebrews 11:3 to Genesis 1:1?
hebreus-cam-hb-04-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews rereads Genesis: God forms the worlds by his word.

feedbackWrong.b: God is the Creator; the visible is the work of his word.
feedbackWrong.c: It is by God's word that faith understands creation.

hebreus-cam-hb-04-06.hint: See the means by which the worlds were formed.

options.a: God creates by the word
options.b: The visible creates God
options.c: Faith dispenses with the word

hebreus-pro-hb-04-01.question: Hebrews 11:4 shows Abel's faith at work in what he offered to God.
hebreus-pro-hb-04-01.feedbackCorrect: Abel's faith did not stay only inside: it offered to God.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse begins with faith and soon shows Abel's offering.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-01.hint: Connect the start of the verse to Abel's action.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-02.question: In Hebrews 11:4, tap the phrase that shows what Abel's sacrifice was like.
hebreus-pro-hb-04-02.feedbackCorrect: Abel's sacrifice was more excellent than his brother's.

feedbackWrong.a: Righteous is the testimony Abel received, not the offering itself.
feedbackWrong.c: Dead speaks of his end, not of what the sacrifice was like.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-02.hint: Compare his offering with his brother's.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-03.question: What reading do Hebrews 11:1–4 support about true faith?
hebreus-pro-hb-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Faith is certain of what it does not see and acts, like Abel when he offered.

feedbackWrong.a: By faith, Abel offered: trust changed his action.
feedbackWrong.b: Abel died without seeing everything, and yet the text approves him.
feedbackWrong.c: Faith is conviction precisely of realities that are not seen.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-03.hint: Put together the definition and the example of Abel.

options.a: It is only a feeling, without changing practice
options.b: It guarantees winning every struggle in this life
options.c: It demands seeing everything before trusting God
options.d: It trusts without seeing and lives from that

hebreus-pro-hb-04-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Hebrews 11:3–4?
hebreus-pro-hb-04-04.feedbackCorrect: From creation by the word, the text arrives at Abel, whose faith still speaks.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with creation; Abel's speech after death closes the passage.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-04.hint: Abel's still speaks is the final point.

options.a: The worlds formed by the word
options.b: Abel offers the excellent sacrifice
options.c: Abel still speaks after death

hebreus-pro-hb-04-05.question: In Hebrews 11:3, the worlds were what by the word of God?
hebreus-pro-hb-04-05.feedbackCorrect: By faith we understand that God formed the worlds by the word.

feedbackWrong.a: Seeing is our limit; forming is what God did.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of forming the worlds, not of touching them.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-05.hint: See the verb tied to the worlds in the verse.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-06.question: What connects Hebrews 11:4 to Genesis 4:4?
hebreus-pro-hb-04-06.feedbackCorrect: Genesis tells of the offering; Hebrews shows the faith behind it.

feedbackWrong.b: God approved Abel's offerings, according to the text itself.
feedbackWrong.c: Hebrews says Abel's offering was more excellent.

hebreus-pro-hb-04-06.hint: See who offers and how God receives it.

options.a: Abel believes and offers to God
options.b: God rejects those who offer
options.c: Cain offers better than Abel

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-01.question: In Hebrews 8:3, every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices.
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Offering gifts and sacrifices is the task given to the high priest.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Hebrews 8:3 about the priest's task.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-01.hint: See the task given to every high priest.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-02.question: In Hebrews 1:4, tap the word that shows the Son's position over the angels.
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-02.feedbackCorrect: He became superior to the angels, with a more excellent name.

feedbackWrong.a: Name is what he inherited; the position comes before that.
feedbackWrong.c: Angels are the ones compared to him, not his position.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-02.hint: Look for the comparison right at the start of the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-03.question: According to Hebrews 4:16, what do we find as help in time of need?
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-03.feedbackCorrect: At the throne of grace, help comes at the moment we need it.

feedbackWrong.a: Help in time of need assumes trial, not its absence.
feedbackWrong.b: Grace leads us back to God, not to stop praying.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of timely help, not of identical answers.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-03.hint: Read the end of the invitation in verse 16.

options.a: Complete absence of any trial
options.b: Strength never to need prayer again
options.c: The same answer for every request
options.d: Grace for the hour of need

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-04.question: Put Hebrews 1:3 in the order of the text.
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-04.feedbackCorrect: Radiance, exact representation and sustaining of everything: in that order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the radiance of glory; the sustaining comes after.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-04.hint: The verse begins with the Son's glory.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-05.question: In Hebrews 11:1, faith is also conviction of what kind of realities?
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-05.feedbackCorrect: Faith is conviction of realities that are not yet seen.

feedbackWrong.b: Doubt is the opposite of both marks of faith in the text.
feedbackWrong.c: Assurance is the first mark, tied to what is hoped for.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-05.hint: It is the second mark, after assurance.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-06.question: What does Hebrews 11:2 say that connects to this context?
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-06.feedbackCorrect: By faith, the ancients gained a good testimony from God.

feedbackWrong.b: The testimony comes precisely from God about those who believed.
feedbackWrong.c: A good testimony is approval, not disapproval of them.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-06.hint: See what the ancients gained by faith.

options.a: Ancients approved by faith
options.b: Faith without God's approval
options.c: Ancients disapproved by faith

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-07.question: In Hebrews 4:16, tap the place of grace we are invited to approach.
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-07.feedbackCorrect: We approach the throne of grace to receive mercy.

feedbackWrong.a: Help is what we find there, not the place itself.
feedbackWrong.b: Grace describes the throne; the named place comes before.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-07.hint: Look for the place after the invitation to approach.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-08.question: Put Hebrews 8:6 in the order of the text.
hebreus-sem-hb-boss-08.feedbackCorrect: Excellent ministry, mediator and better promises: in that order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with his ministry; the promises close the verse.

hebreus-sem-hb-boss-08.hint: The better promises come at the end of the verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-01.question: In Hebrews 1:1, God spoke to the fathers in these last days through the ancient prophets.
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: In these last days God spoke to us through the Son, not through the prophets.

feedbackWrong.true: Swap the final messenger: in the last days, it is the Son who speaks.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-01.hint: Separate the time of the prophets from the time of the Son.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-02.question: In Hebrews 8:6, tap the word that marks the turn to Jesus' ministry.
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-02.feedbackCorrect: That word turns the page from the ancient service to Jesus'.

feedbackWrong.a: Ministry is the new subject, not the marker of the turn.
feedbackWrong.c: Effect accompanies the turn, but it is not the time word.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-02.hint: It is the first word of the verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-03.question: How does Hebrews 4:14–15 support the invitation to approach God?
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-03.feedbackCorrect: In the heavens and compassionate: therefore we come with confidence.

feedbackWrong.b: He was tempted in all things, as we are.
feedbackWrong.c: One comes to receive mercy, before any victory.
feedbackWrong.d: Holding on to the confession goes together with seeking his grace.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-03.hint: Put together his place and his heart for us.

options.a: We have a priest in the heavens who sympathizes
options.b: We have a priest who was never tested
options.c: God answers only those who have already overcome temptation
options.d: A firm confession makes God's help unnecessary

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-04.question: How does the thread of Hebrews advance in this review?
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-04.feedbackCorrect: The speech through the Son comes first; heir and Creator explain it.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the speech in the last days; the universe closes the passage.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-04.hint: The universe made through him comes at the end of verse 2.

options.a: God finally speaks through the Son
options.b: The Son is heir of everything
options.c: He made the universe through him

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-05.question: In Hebrews 4:15, the high priest can do what regarding our weaknesses?
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-05.feedbackCorrect: He can sympathize because he was tempted as we are.

feedbackWrong.b: He knows weaknesses from the inside; he does not forget them.
feedbackWrong.c: Pulling away is the opposite of what the text says about him.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-05.hint: See the verb tied to our weaknesses.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-06.question: What connects Hebrews 1:2 to John 1:3?
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-06.feedbackCorrect: Both texts say everything was made through him.

feedbackWrong.a: Angels worship the Son; the one who made the universe was he.
feedbackWrong.c: Nothing came about on its own: everything was made through the Son.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-06.hint: See through whom everything was made in both.

options.a: The angels created the universe
options.b: Christ made all things
options.c: The universe came about on its own

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-07.question: In Hebrews 4:12, tap the quality of the word that shows it is not dead.
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-07.feedbackCorrect: God's word is living: it acts and discerns the heart.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the second quality, about its effect.
feedbackWrong.b: Sword is the image of comparison, not the quality asked for.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-07.hint: It is the first quality named in the verse.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-08.question: How are the marks of faith linked in Hebrews 11:1–2?
hebreus-cam-hb-boss-08.feedbackCorrect: The two marks of faith appear before the testimony of the ancients.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the marks of faith; the ancients come after.

hebreus-cam-hb-boss-08.hint: The approved ancients close the chain.

options.a: Assurance of what is still hoped for
options.b: Conviction of what is not seen
options.c: Ancients approved for living this way

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-01.question: Hebrews shows Jesus greater than the angels and mediator of a superior covenant.
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Greater than the angels and a superior mediator: that is the thread of the letter.

feedbackWrong.false: Put Hebrews 1:4 together with 8:6 and see the two sides of the argument.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-01.hint: Think about the thread that links the beginning and the middle of the letter.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-02.question: In Hebrews 11:2, tap whom the text presents as living proof of faith.
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-02.feedbackCorrect: The ancients lived the definition and received a good testimony.

feedbackWrong.b: Faith is their path, not the people presented.
feedbackWrong.c: Testimony is what they gained, not who they are.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-02.hint: Look for the people named in the verse.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-03.question: Which reading best sums up Hebrews' final invitation in this review?
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-03.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews' answer is to come with confidence, without shrinking back.

feedbackWrong.a: The covenant in Jesus is superior; it needs no completing with the old.
feedbackWrong.c: One comes to receive mercy, not because one already deserves it.
feedbackWrong.d: The faith of Hebrews perseveres; Abel and the ancients lived it by acting.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-03.hint: Connect his compassion to the throne of grace.

options.a: Going back to the old sacrifices to complete Jesus
options.b: Coming confidently to the one who sympathizes with us
options.c: Waiting to deserve it before seeking God
options.d: Trusting that faith dispenses with any perseverance

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-04.question: Which sequence reveals the complete thread of Hebrews in this review?
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-04.feedbackCorrect: From the greater Son, to the superior covenant, to the faith that perseveres.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the letter: Son, covenant and, finally, the faith that walks.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-04.hint: The faith that perseveres is the letter's point of arrival.

options.a: The greater Son is presented
options.b: He mediates the superior covenant
options.c: Faith perseveres without shrinking back

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-05.question: In Hebrews 8:8, what does God say he will do with the promised new covenant?
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-05.feedbackCorrect: God himself will establish the new covenant with Israel and Judah.

feedbackWrong.a: Breaking is the opposite of the promise God announces here.
feedbackWrong.c: The promise is announced to the people, not hidden from them.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-05.hint: See God's verb about the new covenant.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-06.question: What connects Hebrews 8:8 to Jeremiah 31:31?
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews quotes Jeremiah: the new covenant was promised by God.

feedbackWrong.a: It is a promise being remembered, not the end of promises.
feedbackWrong.b: The promise looks ahead, to Israel and Judah, not only to the past.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-06.hint: See what God promises in both texts.

options.a: The end of every promise
options.b: A covenant only with the fathers
options.c: The promised new covenant

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-07.question: In Hebrews 1:6, tap what the angels must do before the Firstborn.
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-07.feedbackCorrect: All the angels worship the Son presented into the world.

feedbackWrong.a: Firstborn is the one who is worshiped, not what the angels do.
feedbackWrong.b: World is where the Firstborn is presented, not their action.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-07.hint: See God's order to the angels at the end of the verse.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-08.question: Which sequence reveals the path of persevering faith in Hebrews 11?
hebreus-pro-hb-boss-08.feedbackCorrect: Understand, offer and still speak: faith leaves a living testimony.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with understanding creation; Abel's speech closes the path.

hebreus-pro-hb-boss-08.hint: Abel's speech after death is the end of the path.

options.a: By faith we understand creation
options.b: Abel offers to God with faith
options.c: Abel still speaks after dying
